implementation_language.bridge_reason: The browser interaction layer uses the browser's native JavaScript runtime; business rules, site conversion, aggregation, and persistence remain in AFJ.

verification: Candidate site retained the same site_id when converted to OPERATING.
Protected HTTP page and API returned 401 without credentials and 200 with the correct Basic/API key.
Operations create, dashboard, and weekly flows returned expected JSON on an isolated database.

A live isolated preview exposed an AFJ HTTP-boundary bug when vehicle_job_id was nested through parse-int-param; optional relation IDs now pass to domain ownership validation directly, and the linked rework path is covered by the domain test.

Browser feedback exposed a double-auth 401 and CSP-blocked inline handlers; operations APIs now accept either the same Admin Basic credential or x-api-key, all inline event attributes were replaced with delegated listeners, and a data favicon removes the incidental 404.

The keyboard-heavy quick-action modals were replaced with touch-first chips, now-time buttons, steppers, multi-select work chips, and conditional detail panels; a real 390px Chrome run verified 24 vehicle touch controls, zero selects, exact AFJ payload serialization, no overflow, and no runtime errors.

Vehicle condition state is normalized as arrival/final × exterior/interior × canonical checkpoint rows. AFJ validates 10 exterior and 10 interior codes, stores vehicle and conditions transactionally, rolls both back on invalid codes, and returns condition rows in the dashboard.
A 390px Chrome run selected all 10 exterior checkpoints as normal and one interior floor checkpoint as contaminated; exactly 11 of 20 checked rows were serialized, with no overflow or runtime errors.
Full verification passed: 17/17 FreeLang tests, both UI scripts, 73/73 OpenAPI routes, diff check, HTTP security, and DB backup/restore rehearsal.
Desktop 1440x1100 and mobile 390x844 layouts were rendered from the same operations UI and visually inspected before integration.
